label: LC_SLOWGRU_BAKEOFF_QUALIFICATION
note: Eval script used the relative floor3 criterion (retain >=90% of same-step Control). QUALIFIED on the literal bakeoff gate. ABLATION CAVEAT: the long-term slow state is NOT the causal driver of the gain (D_off >= A_on).

slowgru_vs_control.note_vs_baseline: SlowGRU@24576 (42.97%) EXCEEDS the healthy teacher17500 baseline (39.45%) by +3.52pp.

ablation_SR_pp.interpretation: D_off (43.75%) >= A_on (42.97%): disabling the slow channel IMPROVES SR slightly. B_clear (42.19%, h forced to 0 so slow channel contributes nothing) is also ~ A_on. => the +6.64pp gain over Control lives ENTIRELY in the co-trained SHORT-TERM policy; the accumulated slow state contributes ~0 (A_on - B_clear = +0.78pp) and is neutral-to-slightly-harmful (A_on - D_off = -0.78pp).

significance.verdict: MARGINALLY significant: +6.64pp = +17 worlds; McNemar p=0.072 (not <0.05); 95% CI lower bound exactly 0. Much stronger than EventMemory32 but still not below the 0.05 threshold.

memory_engagement.caveat: gate10 KL=6.4e-5 is very small; combined with D_off>=A_on, the slow state is barely used and not beneficial.

SLOWGRU_with_caveat: QUALIFIED on the gate and CLEARLY the stronger performer vs EventMemory32 (+6.64pp vs +1.17pp). BUT the causal ablation shows the gain is from the co-trained short-term policy, NOT the long-term slow state (D_off >= A_on). Advancing SlowGRU as a long-term-memory STRUCTURE is therefore not clearly justified by the mechanism, even though the trained arm is strong.
